content.text:
I'm mapping out an 11x11 grid centered at (5,5), listing which cells hold values 3, 1, and 6, and figuring out which of each group sits closest to the center as an anchor point.

I picked (4,7) as anchor for the 1-cells and (7,5) for the 6-cells, and I'm ordering processing by anchor row: 1 first, then 3, then 6. For each target cell of value 1, I'm tracing a path from the anchor going vertically then horizontally, avoiding protected cells belonging to the 3 and 6 groups, and marking each path cell as 1 — working through targets (0,8), (2,9), (3,0), and (4,7) in turn. Now I'm starting the same process for the 3-cells, treating the 6-cells as protected obstacles to route around.

Continuing the anchor calculations: (6,0) costs 6 with row6 cols0-5 covered, (7,5) is the anchor itself, and (10,0) costs 6 with row10 cols0-5 covered, working through (10,8) next.

Now I'm assembling the final grid row by row, tracking where the 1s, 3s, and 6s land after overwrites — row0 ends up mostly zeros with 3s at columns 3-4 and 1s at 7-8, row1 becomes entirely 6s from column 1 onward after the 6-path overwrites the earlier 3, and row2 mixes 1s, a 3, and a 6.

Continuing through rows 3-8, tracking overlapping 1, 3, and 6 values...

I finish rows 9 and 10, then double-check a few overlaps where the vertical 6-path overwrites earlier 3 or 1 values, confirming rows 5, 6, and 8 at column 5 correctly resolve to 6.

content.text:
I'm mapping out the grid dimensions and cataloging the non-zero cell values by row and column position, working through the layout systematically.

Now I'm computing squared distances from each colored cell to the center point (5,6) for colors 2, 3, 9, 5, and 7, trying to identify which cell of each color is closest to the center and confirming that anchor is uniquely closest for that color.

I've now found the anchors for all five colors and ordered them by distance: color 5 first, then 9, 2, 3, 7. I'm setting up the output as a copy of the input grid, then building a protected set containing all cells belonging to colors 9, 2, 3, and 7 before processing color 5's anchor.

For color 5's targets (1,8), (1,11), (10,4), (10,10), (10,11), I'm tracing paths from the anchor to each target through unprotected cells only, filling row 1 columns 8-11 and column 8 rows 1-10 with color 5 where nothing blocks the path.

After this, row 10 ends up mostly filled with 5s except column 6 which stays protected at 9. Now I need to process color 9's anchor at (3,5), checking which cells around it are protected by other colors like 2, 3, and 7.

I'm working through the fill order for the remaining targets, tracing vertical and horizontal rays from (3,5) to determine which cells get overwritten with 9, being careful to stop at protected cells belonging to lower-numbered colors.

Now moving to anchor (4,4) with protected cells 3 and 7. Working through targets (0,2),(0,6),(2,5),(4,4): tracing col4 rows4→0 and adjusting horizontal spreads from row0, setting values to 2 while respecting the protected cell at (0,3), and similarly propagating 2 through (2,4),(2,5).

Then processing anchor (8,10) with 7 protected cells, sorting targets (0,3),(0,8),(4,12),(8,10),(8,11),(8,12), and tracing col10 downward alongside horizontal spreads from row0 and row4 to fill in distance values of 3 throughout, before starting anchor (9,11) which has no protection.

For that anchor, sorted targets are (9,0),(9,11),(9,12),(10,0),(10,1),(10,12), and tracing both rows 9 and 10 horizontally shows they become entirely filled with 7 since there's no vertical blocking. Now I'm starting to build the actual grid row by row.

Row0 works out to [0,0,2,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,0,0] after applying the propagation from various source cells. For row1, the original zeros get overwritten by the 5-value at (1,8) and (1,11), so columns 8 through 11 become 5.

Working through row1 fully now: applying the 9-values from (1,3) and (1,6) fills columns 3-6, then the 2-value overwrites column 4, giving [0,0,0,9,2,9,9,0,5,5,3,5,0].

For row2, the 5 from the vertical column persists at column 8, the 2-values fill columns 4-5, and the 3-path fills column 10, giving [0,0,0,0,2,2,0,0,5,0,3,0,0]. Now I'm tracing row3, where the 9-value spreads across columns 5-12 while column 4 keeps its 2 from the vertical propagation.

Continuing down through rows 4-8, I'm applying the same overwrite logic: column 5 gets 9, column 8 keeps 5, columns 10-12 get 3 (with row4 having its own 2-3 mix from the diagonal inputs), and rows 5-7 repeat the same pattern before row8 introduces a 9 at column 4 alongside the persisting 5 and 3 values.

Rows 9 and 10 turn out to be entirely filled with 7s across all columns.
